claims.text: The rider cancelled 120 seconds after the driver was assigned, and 120 seconds after the trip was accepted. Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec of the accepted_at timestamp is not chargeable whatever the driver's position, and the record's own platform_policy sets grace_after_match_sec at 180 seconds. The accepted_at is 2026-09-15T15:07:39+08:00 and the cancelled_at is 2026-09-15T15:09:39+08:00 — exactly 120 seconds, inside the 180-second grace. The $4.50 cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The cancellation fee line in the fare breakdown is $4.50 and the payment status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider is presently carrying the disputed charge. POL-NS-10(c) provides that a cancellation fee charged on a cancellation that limb (a) makes non-chargeable is refunded in full with no driver compensation. The amount to be returned is the cancellation-fee line only, $4.50, and no booking or platform fee arises because the trip was never completed.

Independently of the grace, the driver never arrived at the pickup point. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all — arrived_at is null and the events list runs driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled with nothing between. POL-NS-01 limb (a) requires a driver 'arrived' event for the trip, and limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence at or before that event. Neither limb can be satisfied on this record, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the rider is entitled to the refund.

The driver's own trace confirms he was never near the pickup. Across 18 fixes from 15:07:41 to 15:10:31 the driver's minimum distance from the pin is 6833.3 m and his mean distance is 8250.0 m — kilometres away, not metres. The STANDARD arrival radius is 50 m and the wrong-entrance ceiling is 400 m; the driver was more than 17 times the 400 m ceiling away. POL-NS-02 provides that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The driver was still in motion on an expressway when the trip was cancelled, not waiting at a kerb. His 18 fixes report 17 distinct speeds between 57.1 and 62.6 km/h, all far above the 15 km/h motion threshold in POL-NS-05. A driver travelling at 57 to 63 km/h cannot be holding position inside a 50 m arrival radius, and POL-NS-05 treats speed at or above 15 km/h as showing the driver is still in motion. This corroborates that no arrival occurred and no waiting clock ever started.

Even if an arrival marker had been pressed, the dwell would be zero. The derived arrival block reports longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec of 0.0, qualifying_fix_count of 0, and a shortfall_sec of 180.0 against the STANDARD minimum dwell of 180 seconds. POL-NS-06 provides that where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present. The shortfall here is the entire 180 seconds.

The rider's own device was at the pickup point. The rider track carries one fix at 15:10:40 with a distance of 8.8 m from the pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 1. The rider was where the booking said she would be; the driver was 6.8 km away travelling at 60 km/h. The failure to connect is entirely driver-side.

The rider's claim is that she cancelled two minutes after booking because her plans changed. The record bears out the two minutes exactly — 120 seconds from accepted_at to cancelled_at — and the cancellation reason code is RIDER_CANCELLED, not any of the three no-show codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). Limb (d) therefore fails as well, and POL-NS-01's own text states that no Singapore platform's published policy allows a driver to collect a no-show fee on a cancellation recorded under any reason other than the rider's failure to appear.

The rider's profile supports no adverse inference and none is available. Her no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and her disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged. Her prior_disputes_filed and prior_no_show_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not ground any finding. There is no basis to treat this as an abuse case.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING — no advisory covers Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 in this window — and it carries weight 0.0. Its absence is itself citable, and it means POL-NS-06 limb (i) cannot be run to accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals. There are no in-geofence intervals to accumulate in any event: run_count is 0 and longest_run_sec is 0.0. The missing advisory therefore cannot rescue the fee.

The evidence bundle is clean and the deciding facts are carried by artifacts at full weight. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown are all COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes; the trace has 100.0% coverage, a 10 s sample interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0. Nothing in POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d) is engaged, so no down-weighting or escalation under POL-NS-09(e) arises and the refund may issue at full confidence.

The chat log is empty — 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp — and the trip record's chat_message_count is also 0, so the two reconcile and there is no POL-NS-08(c) chat defect. The absence of chat does not help the driver: POL-NS-04 is a rider-exonerating clause and its unavailability simply leaves the fee to be decided on the driver's own evidence, which shows no arrival. POL-NS-11 confirms that an undecidable rider-presence test does not impair the driver's track and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on it.

The driver's profile offers no route to compensation here. His no_show_terminations_30d is 0 and completed_trips_30d is 113, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. But POL-NS-07 only fixes a payout where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither holds, because there was no arrival and the rider cancelled inside the grace. No driver compensation is payable on this record.

The rider filed this dispute and the contested amount is $4.50, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so a refund ruling executes automatically on issue. Under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned; that is the outcome the record supports, with amount_sgd of $4.50 and driver_compensation_sgd null.

ruling.explanation:
The $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider.

WHAT DECIDES IT. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02737) shows accepted_at 2026-09-15T15:07:39+08:00 and cancelled_at 2026-09-15T15:09:39+08:00 — a rider cancellation exactly 120 seconds after acceptance. The record's own platform_policy sets grace_after_match_sec at 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within that grace is not chargeable 'whatever the driver's position', and POL-NS-10(c) requires such a fee to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. POL-NS-10(f) (chargeable late cancellation) is never reached because the cancellation fell inside the grace. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02737) confirms the charged line is the $4.50 cancellation fee, with total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so that is the sum returned. amount_sgd = $4.50, driver_compensation_sgd = null. Because the disputed amount is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, this refund executes automatically on issue.

THE PARTIES AGREE ON THE MERITS AND THE RECORD SUPPORTS THEM. Both briefs argued the same outcome, and each independent route confirms the refund. POL-NS-01/POL-NS-02: the trip record carries arrived_at null and no 'arrived' event at all (the events are driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02737) reports qualifying_fix_count 0 against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, with the driver's minimum distance from the pin 6833.3 m across 18 fixes. The driver therefore never arrived and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) both fail. POL-NS-05: the driver's distinct speeds run 57.1–62.6 km/h, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold, and his closest approach (6833.3 m) is more than 17 times the 300 m marker threshold — but there is no arrival marker to falsify, so POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral does not fire, and no referral is produced. POL-NS-06: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 180 s STANDARD minimum, a shortfall of 180 s; the fee is not chargeable on that route alone. POL-NS-01 limb (d) also fails: the cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_CANCELLED, not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. No compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 fixes a payout only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither holds. The driver's profile (EV-DPROF-02737: no_show_terminations_30d 0, completed_trips_30d 113) shows the anti-farming check does not trip, so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged — but that only means no withholding ground exists, not that any payout arises.

RIDER PRESENCE AND PROFILE. The rider's device was at the pin (EV-GPS-02737 rider track: one fix, 8.8 m from the pickup, inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius), which corroborates that the failed pickup was not her doing; POL-NS-04 is in any event a rider-exonerating route and is not needed here, and per POL-NS-11 a rider-presence question that could not be run would not impair the driver's track or lower confidence in a finding resting on it. The profile points raised under POL-GEN-01 carry no adverse inference: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d and disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged, and the remaining fields (rating, account_age_days, prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags, etc.) are context-only and were correctly not used as grounds. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is met: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifact contradicts another on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and the sole evidence for the deciding fact is not impaired.

EVIDENCE INTEGRITY. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes; the trace has 100% coverage, a 10 s cadence, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, and the empty chat log reconciles with chat_message_count 0, so POL-NS-08 limbs (a)–(d) are not engaged. The deciding facts (acceptance time, cancellation time, grace period and fee charged) are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no artifact caps confidence below the floor.

DISCARDED CLAIMS. Two claims — one from each side — argued from the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02737-01 at weight 0.0 without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and were discarded under POL-GEN-02(1). Their substance does not change the outcome: POL-NS-06 limb (i) could only ever permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and the trace shows run_count 0 and longest_run_sec 0.0, so there were no intervals to accumulate. The single referee warning (a rider claim naming prior_disputes_filed and prior_no_show_flags) is not a discard: the claim correctly treated those fields as context-only and argued they cannot ground a finding.

The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown are all COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes; the trace has 100.0% coverage, a 10 s sample interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0. Nothing in POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d) is engaged, so no down-weighting or escalation under POL-NS-09(e) arises and the refund may issue at full confidence.

The chat log is empty — 0 messages, no first or last message timestamp — and the trip record's chat_message_count is also 0, so the two reconcile and there is no POL-NS-08(c) chat defect. The absence of chat does not help the driver: POL-NS-04 is a rider-exonerating clause and its unavailability simply leaves the fee to be decided on the driver's own evidence, which shows no arrival. POL-NS-11 confirms that an undecidable rider-presence test does not impair the driver's track and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on it.

The driver's profile offers no route to compensation here. His no_show_terminations_30d is 0 and completed_trips_30d is 113, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. But POL-NS-07 only fixes a payout where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither holds, because there was no arrival and the rider cancelled inside the grace. No driver compensation is payable on this record.

The rider filed this dispute and the contested amount is $4.50, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so a refund ruling executes automatically on issue. Under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned; that is the outcome the record supports, with amount_sgd of $4.50 and driver_compensation_sgd null.

The rider cancelled 120 seconds after the driver was assigned, and the trip record shows the driver had not arrived: arrived_at is null, there is no 'arrived' event, and the only events are driver_assigned, driver_en_route and trip_cancelled. Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec of accepted_at is not chargeable whatever the driver's position, and the record carries grace_after_match_sec of 180 seconds. The cancellation at 15:09:39 is 120 seconds after accepted_at at 15:07:39, inside the grace, so the $4.50 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The driver never arrived at the pickup point. The GPS trace's derived arrival block shows driver_fix_count of 18 but qualifying_fix_count of 0 and longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec of 0.0, and the driver's minimum distance from the pickup pin across the whole trace is 6833.3 m. Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only where the trace contains at least 3 consecutive fixes within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and here there are none, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

Even setting the grace period aside, the effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for this STANDARD zone class, a shortfall of 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full where the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, whether or not the rider was present. The trace shows no in-geofence interval at all, so the shortfall is total.

The driver's own track shows him travelling at 57.1 to 62.6 km/h throughout the trace, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold, and his closest approach to the pin was 6833.3 m, far beyond the 300 m mark. Under POL-NS-05 the arrival marker is false and does not start the waiting clock; here there is no arrival marker at all and no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, so the fee is refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable.

The rider's own device was stationary at the pickup point: the rider track shows a single fix at 0.0 km/h with a distance of 8.8 m from the pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius. The rider was where the booking said she would be, and the driver was 6.8 km away. This corroborates that the failure to complete the pickup was not the rider's doing.

The fare breakdown confirms the $4.50 cancellation fee was charged and remains charged, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The rider's claim is that she was charged despite cancelling two minutes after booking, and the ledger shows exactly that charge standing. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND returns the whole contested amount to the filing party, and the contested amount is the $4.50 cancellation fee.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no advisory covers this pickup road in this window. Under POL-NS-06 limb (i) a traffic advisory is required to be present and populated before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed, and a MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable. The absence is citable and it means the driver cannot rely on any kerb restriction or enforcement operation to excuse the total absence of in-geofence dwell.
